topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening administrative framing and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Endogenous, Genetic, and Environmental Drivers of Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer etiology, balancing intrinsic mutational processes and genetics against environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the role of infectious organisms in cancer development, with a detailed focus on Epstein-Barr virus and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens interact with cellular metabolism to induce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Contextual Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro approaches used to evaluate and confirm the carcinogenicity of exposures.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic serves as the closing framing of the lecture, summarizing the main conclusions and discussing real-world risk-benefit evaluations.
